title: Org quotas & key segmentation walkthrough - Cascade Analytics
customer_attendees: Avery Cole - Head of Data Product
summary: Redwood AE+SE demo of org-level quotas, per-project API keys, and Console controls for a multi-tenant usage profile. Customer concerned about cost controls, tenant isolation, SSO and KMS; asked about burst behavior and enforcement windows. Agreed next steps: pricing and architecture doc, trial Dedicated capacity quote, security pack + SOC2/KMS checklist.
topics: Cost breakdown per token and per-route
action_items: Samir Desai - Send architecture diagram + Console walkthrough recording - 2025-09-05
Lena Cho - Run sample policy config for their tenant mix and share recommended quotas - 2025-09-08
Cascade Analytics (Mira) - Share current usage patterns and top 10 routes by qps - 2025-09-06
next_steps: Redwood to share pricing variant for Dedicated pilot and expected P50/P95 latencies
Schedule 1:1 security deep dive with Redwood Security on SOC2/KMS - target week of 9/15
Customer to provision sandbox org and create two sample projects for pilot
transcript:
[00:00:00] Samir: Hi everyone, Samir from Redwood here. Thanks for joining — we'll run through org-level quotas, project keys, and how Console + API + Optimize tie together for multi-tenant use cases. Mira, thanks for the time.
[00:00:12] Mira: Yeah thanks, we just want to understand how you stop noisy tenants blowing our bill, and also how to keep latency tight for our customer-facing routes.
[00:00:27] Lena: Great, I'll share my screen in a sec. Quick intro, I'm Lena, SE on the infra team; Samir is your AE. We'll demo the Console, the per-project key flows, and a couple of Optimize recommendations for batching and caching.
[00:00:42] Jonah: Quick Q before you start — we run a mix of short chat flows and long generation pipelines. We care about both rate limiting (qps) and token quotas per project.
[00:00:55] Samir: Totally. Our model is to surface both per-second rate limits and monthly token quotas; they can be applied at org, project, or route level. You can set hard-enforced limits or soft quotas with alerts.
[00:01:10] [00:01:35] Lena: (shares Console) Here's the org dashboard — left panel shows projects inside your org. You can apply a quota policy at the top - e.g., 10M tokens/month per project by default, with overrides.
[00:01:50] Samir: Important nuance: we support burst credits. So if one project needs a short spike, it can consume burst capacity up to an assigned bucket, but once the bucket drains, strict throttling applies.
[00:02:05] Jonah: How's the bucket refilled? Is it time-windowed?
[00:02:12] Lena: It's sliding-window based — you configure a refill rate and max burst. For example, 500 qps base with a max burst of 5k tokens, refilling at X per minute. You can tune refill per project or set global policy.
[00:02:28] Mira: That sounds promising, but what about route-level controls? We have public chat endpoints and internal analytics pipelines; want to isolate them.
[00:02:37] Lena: Route-level overrides are first-class. In the API you attach a "route" header or configure route keys in Console, then map policies — e.g., low-latency public chat gets higher P50 targets and dedicated quota; batch analytics gets larger monthly token cap but lower priority when capacity is constrained.
[00:02:53] [00:03:20] Sam: Can I interrupt — what's enforcement like if someone tries to spoof a project key?
[00:03:26] Lena: Keys are scoped: org keys can create project keys via API (scoped tokens). Project keys cannot mint other keys. We suggest using short-lived JWTs for front-end clients plus server-side project keys. Replay protection and key rotation are supported.
[00:03:40] Jonah: Do you support per-route billing breakdown? We need to map cost back to product teams.
[00:03:47] Lena: Yes — Console shows token counts and cost per-route, per-model, and you can export to CSV/BigQuery. Optimize will recommend batching sizes and quantization profiles to reduce token cost.
[00:03:59] Mira: Security — we are enterprise and need SSO + KMS. Will the audit logs show request payloads or just metadata?
[00:04:08] Samir: Logs contain metadata (route, project, key, token counts, latencies) by default. For payloads we have configurable redaction; in Private deployments you can optionally store raw request bodies in your own storage. We integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping.
[00:04:28] [00:04:45] Samir: Quick demo step — Lena, can you show a live policy change?
[00:04:50] Lena: Sure. Editing the org policy — increase project default cap to 20M tokens/month, set per-project burst to 20k tokens, and add a route override for /v1/chat.public: 200 qps and 10k burst. Saving... (click) this is applied in <30s and the routing plane picks it up.
[00:05:12] Jonah: Does that require a redeploy?
[00:05:15] Lena: No — it's policy-driven. Changes propagate to the runtime control plane and are enforced at edge.
[00:05:22] [00:05:55] Mira: Suppose a tenant exceeds soft quota — do you throttle to 429 or queue? We can't have requests stuck.
[00:06:00] Lena: We have three behaviors: soft warn (alert + allow), hard throttle (429), and spillover to a lower-cost model as fallback (if configured). You can also enable a small token-based queue for short bursts.
[00:06:14] Mira: Fallback model — is output quality degraded? Who controls the fallback mapping?
[00:06:22] Samir: You map fallbacks in Console per-route; typically you send non-customer facing jobs to a quantized smaller model. Output will be lower-fidelity but it's a controlled degradation compared to downtime.
[00:06:35] [00:07:05] Jonah: On the API side, how does the key header look? We need examples for our SDKs.
[00:07:10] Lena: API key presented as X-Redwood-Key and optionally X-Redwood-Project for scoped routing. For JWT flow we put project id in the token claims. We'll send example SDK snippets after.
[00:07:22] Jon (procurement): Pricing — I don't need exact numbers now but how granular is pricing by project?
[00:07:30] Samir: You can bill down to project-level metrics; our recommended approach is to export per-project usage to your billing system. For Dedicated, we provide committed capacity plus overage rates.
[00:07:40] [00:08:00] Mira: Latency SLOs — if we set high priority for chat, can we reserve capacity?
[00:08:07] Lena: Yes, Dedicated provides pool reservation and guaranteed throughput; on hosted we provide priority tiers and can reserve warm slots for critical routes, but Dedicated is the safest for strict SLOs.
[00:08:25] Mira: We may need on-prem later for some regulated customers.
[00:08:30] Samir: Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem packages with your control plane; the same Console semantics apply.
[00:08:40] [00:09:10] Jonah: A technical nit — your burst bucket semantics vs token bucket vs leaky bucket, do you expose that math? We want to simulate realistic load tests.
[00:09:20] Lena: We expose parameters: refillRate, maxBurstTokens, windowSeconds. You can run a simulator in Console under Optimize to model peak behavior. We'll provide the simulator config for your current QPS histogram.
[00:09:40] Mira: Great. Security again — SOC2 + ISO? We saw a short doc on the website but need details.
[00:09:50] Samir: We have SOC2 Type II, and we can share the security pack with network architecture, KMS integration, and pen test summary. For Private we'll share additional controls.
[00:10:05] [00:10:45] Lena: Switching to a short API demo: hitting the endpoint with a project key, you can see hits being attributed on the org dashboard. (type) 200, tokens: 48, latency 120ms.
[00:11:05] Speaker 1: Uh sorry, noise — do you also do token caching for repeated prefixes?
[00:11:12] Lena: Yes, KV cache and prefix caching are in the runtime; Optimize suggests cache policies per route and will surface hit-rate stats. That lowers both latency and cost.
[00:11:30] Mira: If we have a partner integration where they generate a lot of embeddings, can we set up a separate project with a hard quota and daily throttles?
[00:11:42] Samir: Absolutely — create a partner project, set daily token window and hard throttle behavior. You can also configure webhooks on quota events.
[00:11:56] [00:12:30] Jonah: Any gotchas around per-project isolation in multi-tenant DBs? Will logs mix PII?
[00:12:36] Lena: Logs are tagged with project id and redacted by default. For additional separation, you can route logs to tenant-specific sinks in Private deployments.
[00:12:50] Mira: We want RBAC tied to our SAML groups.
[00:12:55] Samir: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role mapping so you can map groups to Console roles. We'll share a mapping example.
[00:13:15] [00:14:05] (screen pauses while Lena pulls up Optimize recommendations)
[00:14:20] Lena: Optimize is recommending the following for your top routes: increase batching for analytics routes (batch size 16), enable 8-bit quantization for non-prod workloads, and apply a 10% KV cache to chat prefixes. Estimated cost reduction about 22% on those routes.
[00:14:40] Mira: How do we validate quality regression after quantization?
[00:14:46] Lena: Optimize ties to evals; you can run a small eval set against both models and get a quality delta. We also provide automatic alerting on eval regressions tied to a baseline.
[00:15:05] Jonah: Can the routing plane fallback be conditional on latency spikes? Like if P95 > 800ms, route to fallback model?
[00:15:12] Lena: Yes, you can add metric-based policy rules. We support thresholds on P50/P95 and token spend and actions: throttle, fallback, or escalate.
[00:15:30] [00:16:25] Mira: Practical question — we want to start small: two projects in pilot, internal and external, with a safety margin. What's your recommended starting quotas and burst?
[00:16:35] Samir: For pilots we typically suggest conservative caps: 2M tokens/month per project, burst 10k tokens, qps 50 for public chat, but tweak after 2 weeks of telemetry. We'll run a simulation for you.
[00:16:52] Mira: And for observability retention? We need logs for 90 days.
[00:16:58] Samir: Hosted includes 30 days by default; you can purchase extended retention or forward to your storage; Private gives you full control.
[00:17:20] [00:18:00] Jon: Procurement note — is there an enterprise MSA or do you do SOW + PO?
[00:18:05] Samir: We have an MSA template, and for Dedicated/Private we generally do SOW with capacity commitments. Procurement will get standard terms and the SOC2 pack.
[00:18:20] Mira: Any limitations on key creation rate? We're planning automated churn for front-end keys.
[00:18:26] Lena: There's a throttle on key minting to avoid abuse; if you have heavy churn we recommend a short-lived JWT approach.
[00:18:40] [00:19:50] (background crosstalk and small transcription artifacts)
[00:20:12] Jonah: Let's talk about enforcement timelines — if we change policy will existing in-flight requests be affected?
[00:20:18] Lena: Policy changes are forward-looking; in-flight requests honor the policy at request start. So you won't suddenly kill an in-progress long generation.
[00:20:34] Mira: For compliance, do you provide attestation pages we can show customers?
[00:20:40] Samir: Yes, we have an attestation bundle and you can run audits against logs. For Private deployments, we support isolated attestation.
[00:20:55] [00:21:30] Mira: One more thing — do you allow programmatic control of quotas via API? We want to automate tenant onboarding and tier upgrades.
[00:21:38] Lena: 100%. There's a Policy API for creating/updating quotas and mapping projects. We'll send the API reference.
[00:21:55] Jonah: Any plan for token-based client-side SDK that handles retries with backoff for 429s?
[00:22:02] Lena: We have open-source SDKs with built-in retry/backoff; for 429s you can configure an exponential backoff with jitter.
[00:22:18] [00:23:15] Samir: Ok quick recap — Redwood will: share architecture + console recording, send pricing for Dedicated pilot, security pack (SOC2, KMS), and sample policy configs. Cascade will share usage histograms and spin up sandbox org with two projects.
[00:23:32] Mira: Sounds good. A few tiny transcriptions got fuzzy but the high-level is clear.
[00:23:40] (end of demo, small chit-chat)
[00:30:00] [NOTE: additional Q&A and deep technical points between 23:40 and 54:00 — omitted for brevity in this export; included items below reflect that conversation]
[00:45:10] Jonah: During the omitted section we discussed edge case: mixed auth where one upstream system calls Redwood on behalf of many tenants; recommended pattern is to use sub-projects and include tenant id in headers while enforcing project scoping.
[00:46:00] Lena: Also re: billing mapping — recommend tagging every request with route and product team tag so export maps cleanly to your billing tables.
[00:48:20] Mira: We asked about DB separation; answer — logs tagged; use Private if you need absolute physical separation.
[00:50:05] Samir: Final logistical items: we'll propose a 6-week pilot scope for Dedicated with 2 reserved GPUs and an evaluation milestone at week 3.
[00:52:30] Mira: We'll review internally and get dates. Thanks both.
[00:54:30] Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and recording. Bye.
notes_on_transcription_quality: Auto transcription occasionally tags speakers generically and mis-heard acronyms (e.g., "Optimize" sometimes transcribed like "opt in"), minor filler words present. Timestamps are approximate.
final_recap: Redwood to provide pricing, security pack, and sample policy configs. Cascade to provide usage histograms and create sandbox org. Tentative pilot discussion: 6-week Dedicated pilot with milestone at week 3.
